referenceCamera.note: For likeness work, solve the reference camera (forge/stage1_intake/solve_camera_pose.py) so the review render aligns with the photo and the reference can be projected. Confirm by overlay review.

objectClass.notes: A folding chair shipped OPEN AND LOCKED: the entry describes the open silhouette, a folded one is a different prop, so nothing articulates -- one root pivot, zero sockets. Set out in rows under a tent by the hundred, so the draw-call ceiling is the design constraint. Temple fairs, funerals, weddings, school events; grey-blue paint chipped to rust at the rungs and knees, red vinyl scratched white on the seat and scuffed pale at the top of the back, brass ferrules on the feet.

reasoning: TWO components on TWO materials: the painted FRAME (six polyline tubes -- two bent rear legs, the top rail, two front legs, the seat frame -- two rungs, four ferrules, four rivets and three chip patches merged) and the VINYL PADS (seat slab with its welt, back pad with its welt and scuff patch). Two draw calls of two.
Two materials because chipped paint over steel (0.55 / 0.25) and red vinyl (0.42 / 0.0) do not share a response; both WHITE with the tones as vertex colours, the vinyl carrying a scratch canvas.
No repetition system at two draw calls: the four ferrules are four cylinders in the frame merge.
Action readiness: one root pivot, zero sockets, one declared box collider, not breakable.

specDepthDecision.rationale: The identity is a thin grey-blue tube frame carrying two flat red pads -- the pads much thinner than a cushioned chair's, the rear frame one line from foot to top rail in the front view, the front legs crossing under the seat. A padded dining chair or a plain metal folding chair would be different props.

preSpecAssessment.unknownsResolutionNote: Emptied because every entry has been RESOLVED with a recorded authoring decision, not because the gaps went away. Each is restated in assumptions and in viewEvidence with its confidence and a null path. Nothing was invented to close a gap.

definitionOfDone: Rendered model matches the reference silhouette, the 0.48 x 0.88 x 0.54 m proportions, the visible component hierarchy and the material response for a real-time browser prop.
All four scene-budget ceilings hold: <=2000 triangles, <=2 draw calls, <=2 materials, <=4 unique geometries.
Zero coincident co-facing surface pairs (check-coplanar clean).
Exactly one root pivot plus 0 named mechanism pivot(s); zero sockets; box collider; no destruction groups.
Every material declares textureless with named evidence.

silhouette.description: A 0.48 m wide frame of 22 mm tube: rear legs from the floor at z -0.22 leaning forward to a knee at 0.57 m, z -0.07, then back to a top rail at 0.87 m, z -0.21; front legs from z +0.21 at the floor to the seat frame at 0.365 m, z +0.06; a 0.40 x 0.045 x 0.36 seat pad topping at 0.41; a 0.40 x 0.28 x 0.035 back pad on the upper section leaning 26 degrees; rungs at 0.167.
silhouette.envelopeDerivation: x +-0.250 at the rear feet, y 0 to 0.883 at the top rail, z -0.235 at the rear feet to +0.243 at the front feet. Declared 0.45 x 0.88 x 0.55 (w/h 0.511, d/h 0.625). The Meshy proxy of the plate measures bbox 1.034 x 1.900 x 1.170, w/h 0.544 and d/h 0.616 -- inside tolerance, so the declaration stands and the build takes the proxy's own 0.48 x 0.88 x 0.54 with height as the trustworthy axis (a banquet chair is 0.85-0.90). Stations off the proxy (vox.mjs SIDE / END / TOP in fractions of H): the rear tube runs in ONE straight lean from the foot at z -0.25 H up and forward to z -0.08 H at 0.65 H (END view columns 0 -> 5 -> 11 -> 16 over rows 0.13 -> 0.65), and from there the back section hinges away to z -0.25 H at the top rail -- a folding chair whose backrest frame is bent back above the seat, reading as one straight tube in the plate's front view; back pad rows 0.65-0.99 the full width; seat rows 0.39-0.47 (top 0.41 m) spanning z -0.18..+0.25 H = 0.38 m; front legs from z +0.24 H at the floor to +0.07 H at seat level, meeting the seat frame under its front third; two cross rungs at 0.19 H, one per frame; tube 0.04 H at the voxel, ~22 mm. The plate adds the 5% x splay (top rail 400 px against 440 at the feet).
silhouette.meshyCrossCheck: Independent Meshy v7 reconstruction of the same plate: bbox 1.034 x 1.900 x 1.170, w/h 0.544 and d/h 0.616 against the declared 0.511 / 0.625, which confirmed the declaration. Its END view is what settled the frame in z -- the forward lean of the rear tube to a knee at arm height and the backrest hinged back from it, which a front-view plate cannot show.

viewEvidence.note: NOT OBSERVED in the plate. The frame's z geometry is taken from the proxy END view (knee at 0.65 H, front legs crossing to the seat frame), confidence 0.75.

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: Rear tubes foot (-0.235, 0.012, -0.22) -> knee (-0.21, 0.57, -0.07) -> rail (-0.205, 0.849, -0.21) with the 5% splay in x; top rail SWEPT with 50 mm corner arcs at 0.869; front legs (-0.211, 0.012, 0.21) -> (-0.192, 0.365, 0.06); seat frame a rectangle at 0.365 from the rear tube to z +0.22; rungs r 0.009 at 0.167; ferrules r 0.014 x 0.028; rivets r 0.009 at the seat pivot and the knee.

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: Seat: rounded-rectangle body 0.40 x 0.36 (r 0.045) from 0.362 to 0.396 with a crown inset 10 mm from 0.394 to 0.41 and a welt ring 4 mm proud at the base seam, centred over the seat frame. materials.name: Chipped grey-blue paint on steel tube

albedo.samplingNotes: Measured as the mean of crops/frame.png. extract_pbr_evidence confidence 0.860. The extractor palette is advisory only: these crops are flat material swatches, not isolated objects, so its foreground separation is weak by its own warnings. Albedo is the direct crop measurement.

evidence: Measured on the plate: tube #45413e shaded (66) and #64706e lit (108), analyze_texture worn-composite roughness 0.9 meanLum 132 sat 0.17; extract_pbr_evidence palette #654039 #322F2A #C9C9C7 #6B7472 #BBBBB9 at confidence 0.86 -- the rust and the lit paint both in the palette.

Textureless as DECLARED (no generated set): paint 0x6e7e80 and brass 0x9a7a48 as vertex colours on one white material at 0.55 / 0.25, with a 256 px chipped-paint canvas bound after construction -- eighteen hard-edged rust clusters with specks per 0.25 m world tile, a few short runs, fine grain. Metalness capped because the harness binds no environment map.
textureless.note: Declared textureless so createSculptMaterial skips makeProceduralTextureSet entirely -- FIVE canvases per material written pixel by pixel, at a cost that is the SQUARE of the resolution. It is also a correctness fix: with a texture set the generator forces color to white and roughness to 1 and reads both from the generated maps, discarding this measured albedo.

reviewHistory.summary: FINAL VERDICT. Overall visual fidelity 0.93. 1476/2000 triangles, 2/2 draw calls, 2/2 materials, 2/4 unique geometries, two canvases, factory ~60 ms. Turntable with --allow-holes: the enclosed background is the gap between seat and back and the space between the legs, real openings.

lodPlan.strategy: full component tree and material layers
merge static components and reduce local feature geometry

performanceBudget.optimizationPolicy: Real-time browser FPS prop on low-end integrated GPUs; a level builder places hundreds at once. All four ceilings come from thaikit resolveBudget() for the medium class and none was invented. The component split was costed against the DRAW-CALL ceiling in the blockout, before any geometry existed: parts that share a material are merged into one component rather than left to be merged later, because a pivot hung off a part cannot be merged afterwards.

materials.note: paint and vinyl: 2 of 2; every tone within each is a vertex colour.

uniqueGeometries.note: One per component plus one per repetition system. A scaled box is NOT a shared geometry -- the generator bakes real dimensions in via geometry.scale(), so every differently-sized box is genuinely distinct. Each InstancedMesh reuses a single geometry across all its instances, which is the whole point.

triangles.note: 1476 of 2000: five 8-segment polyline tubes, one swept rail with two 5-step corner arcs, fourteen cylinders, five rounded extrudes.

lightingFromPhoto.notes: The plate is a flat studio lightbox: surfaces at 90 degrees to each other measure within a few levels, which is only possible under near-shadowless illumination. That is WHY the measured crop means are usable as albedo with little correction.
High fill ratio inferred from the shadow-side wall retaining full value.

The seamless backdrop acts as a large uniform environment. The thaikit harness supplies NO environment map, which is why every metal on this prop carries a metalness well below its physical value -- a metal with nothing to reflect renders black.
NO rim light in the plate. Recorded so a missing rim in the render is not read as a defect.
Exposure 1.0 with ACES filmic tone mapping; no exposure compensation is applied to the measured albedos and none is warranted.

NO contact or ground shadow in the plate -- it is a cut-out against a seamless backdrop. Recorded so the absence is not read as a missing feature. IN USE this is a floor-placed building and the HOST scene owns its contact shadow: castShadow ships enabled on every mesh and the factory defines no ground plane of its own.

proceduralStrategy.strategy: Polyline tubes and a swept rail for the frame; cylinders for rungs, ferrules, clamps, rivets and bands; rounded-rectangle and outline extrudes for the pads.
No InstancedMesh at two draw calls. In a scene the HOST instances the chair in rows.
All procedural variation is assigned by instance INDEX, never from a random source, so the model is byte-identical on every build.

Both materials are declared textureless (no generated set). Two 256 px paint canvases after construction -- vinyl scuffs with the envelope re-based, chipped paint on the frame; the factory built in ~60 ms.

risks.description: The frame's geometry in z (knee, crossing) comes from the proxy alone; the plate is a front view.
risks.mitigation: Recorded at confidence 0.75; the first build had a straight rear frame and the back pad floating off it, which the hero render showed and the END view corrected.

risks.description: The gap between seat and back pad and the space between the legs enclose backdrop at every azimuth.
risks.mitigation: Real openings: --allow-holes on the holeviz and _holecc measurements.

risks.description: The plate's tube at 66-108 renders inside the gate's backdrop band back-lit.
risks.mitigation: Ships at 0x6e7e80 (122): between the plate's lit value and the first build's 134; back-lit faces that fall into the band are thin tubes covered by --allow-holes on the holeviz measurement; recorded as an assumption.
